results.title: Creality debuts SPARKX i7 and AI tools at CES 2026 - Engineering.com
results.content:
Creality also introduced the SPARKX i7 at CES and announced its launch. The desktop printer features updated lighting and an out-of-box, ready-to-use setup intended to simplify the printing process for general users.

SPARKX i7 includes a quick-swap hotend intended to simplify maintenance, a redesigned color-changing mechanism and a four-color filament system intended to reduce material waste. It also includes AI-based features for model generation, printing assistance and real-time mobile control. After its CES appearance, pre-orders have opened in North America, with broader availability planned globally. [...] Alongside SPARKX i7, Creality showcased other products in its desktop ecosystem spanning 3D printing, laser engraving, 3D scanning and AI-based creation tools. These included the Ender-3 V4 3D printer, the Falcon T1 laser engraver, the Sermoon P1 3D scanner with blue-laser scanning and Wi-Fi 7 connectivity, and CubeMe, a Creality Cloud feature that generates a customized 3D model from a single photo. results.title: Creality presents multi-tool creation ecosystem and new hardware range at RAPID + TCT 2026 | VoxelMatters - The heart of additive manufacturing
results.content:
Creality presents multi-tool creation ecosystem and new hardware range at RAPID + TCT 2026

Creality presents multi-tool creation ecosystem and new hardware range at RAPID + TCT 2026

The brand’s laser engraving range was also represented with the latest addition, the Falcon T1, on show. Creality is positioning the model as the world’s first five-in-one laser workstation, and it combines 20W diode, 40W diode, 60W MOPA (Master Oscillator Power Amplifier), 20W fiber, and 5W UV laser modules within a single enclosure. Operating at 10,000 mm/s galvo speed with 0.001 mm precision and carrying a Class 1 safety rating.

A more compact model, the Falcon A1C, targets home users with three interchangeable modules — 5W and 10W diode and 1.2W infrared — and support for over 300 materials. [...] Creality took full advantage of its appearance at RAPID + TCT 2026 in Boston this week to present its broad hardware and software portfolio spanning 3D printing, 3D scanning, laser processing, filament recycling, and cloud-based management.

The company’s end-to-end workflow line-up, which connects each stage of the manufacturing process from physical object capture through to finished part production, was in full demo mode as it gave the North American market a hands-on opportunity to see its range – including recent launches – up close. [...] Among the hardware on display was the SPARKX i7, which was officially launched at CES in Las Vegas at the start of the year. The fused filament fabrication (FFF) printer features a quick-swap hotend, a redesigned color-changing mechanism, and a four-color filament system to serve up a desktop configuration that reduces material waste. The printer supports AI-assisted model generation, print monitoring, and mobile operation.

Creality also presented the Filament Maker M1 and Shredder R1, launched on Indiegogo earlier this month, and which it claims is the first integrated desktop system designed to recycle waste plastic and produce custom filament. The crowdfunding campaign for the product has to date raised just under HK$45 million ( $5.7m).
